title: Ordinary marked uniformization reduces to normal complete local schemes
statement:
Use $U(S,Z)$ from [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. For every integer $d\ge0$ the following implication holds. Suppose $U(\operatorname{Spec}A,Z)$ holds for every nonzero normal complete Noetherian local domain $A$ of Krull dimension at most $d$ and every nowhere dense closed subset $Z\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$. Then $U(S,Z)$ holds for every reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $S$ of Krull dimension at most $d$ and every nowhere dense closed subset $Z\subset S$. There is also an unbounded version: if the complete-local hypothesis holds in every finite dimension, then $U(S,Z)$ holds for every reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $S$, without assuming that $S$ has finite global Krull dimension.

Here Noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], quasi-excellent means having an affine open cover by spectra of quasi-excellent rings [def-exc-excellent-ring], normal means integrally closed in the fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and complete means complete for the maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Expose II Proposition 4.3.3, pp.33--34; III Proposition 6.2 and its proof, pp.43--45 (ordinary-alt alternative); VII 2.1--2.3, p.81, for the bounded dimension reduction. No invertible prime is needed in the ordinary alternative.

proof.text: First consider a normal excellent henselian Noetherian local domain $B$ of dimension at most $d$, and a nowhere dense closed $W\subset S_B=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The preparation theorem gives a normal Noetherian local domain $\widehat B$ and nowhere dense $\widehat W$; the completion-dimension theorem gives $\dim\widehat B=\dim B\leq d$. The hypothesis therefore supplies an ordinary alteration cover $(\widehat X_i\to\widehat S_B)_i$ with integral regular sources and the marked boundaries. Apply marked finite-diagram approximation to obtain a model containing all boundary components and intersections and a congruence threshold ensuring regular marked neighborhoods of the whole closed fibres. Apply ordinary cover approximation to that very model; increase the index and take the maximum of the two thresholds. The latter lemma ensures that the reduced dominant parts of every sufficiently close specialization form an ordinary covering.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, p.44, completion and simultaneous approximation; III 3.1(ii), 5.4

proof.text: Choose a section meeting both thresholds as follows. The finite type model algebra has a presentation $B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ by the Noetherian finite-presentation lemma. Its inclusion in $\widehat B$ is a simultaneous solution of the $f_j$. Excellence includes the G-ring condition. Apply henselian-pair approximation to $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ and the common threshold $N\geq1$. The resulting solution in $B$ defines a $B$-algebra map $u$ from the model algebra, congruent to the inclusion modulo $\mathfrak m_B^N\widehat B$; congruence on the generators implies congruence on every polynomial and hence on every element. Thus the same $u$ preserves the entire finite marking diagram. Denote its specialized sources by $M_i$ and their reduced dominant parts by $P_i$. Step 1 gives a finite ordinary cover $(P_i\to S_B)_i$ and regular marked opens $V_i\subset M_i$ containing the whole closed fibres, with $O_i=V_i\cap P_i$ open and closed in $V_i$. Hence each $O_i$ is regular and has the restricted boundary with the prescribed support.

source.place: III section 2, pp.35--36, and Proposition 6.2, pp.44--45; Stacks smoothing.tex Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair), case (2)

proof.text: To retain covering after this shrinking, apply ordinary proper refinement to $(P_i\to S_B)_i$. Obtain an integral proper surjective $p:P\to S_B$, finite generically, and a finite open cover $(P_j)$ with maps $P_j\to P_{i(j)}$. Let $P_j^0$ be the inverse image of $O_{i(j)}$ and $P^0=\bigcup_jP_j^0$. Every point over the closed point $s_B$ lies in some $P_j$ and maps into $O_{i(j)}$, so $P^0$ contains the whole closed fibre. By the definition of proper, $p(P\setminus P^0)$ is closed and misses $s_B$. A nonempty closed subset of the spectrum of a local ring contains its closed point; thus this image is empty and $P^0=P$. The opens $P_j^0$ cover $P$ and factor through the $O_i$. Since $p$ and this open cover are covering generators, the sieve generated by the $O_i$ is covering by transitivity of the topology. This proves that $(O_i\to S_B)_i$ is an ordinary alteration cover.

source.place: II Proposition 4.1.1 and its proof, p.31; III Proposition 6.2, p.44 (ordinary-alt shrinking)

proof.text: The finite type $B$-schemes $M_i$ are Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma, hence their open subschemes $O_i$ are Noetherian. Replace each $O_i$ by its nonempty connected components. There are finitely many: its finitely many irreducible components partition into finitely many connected unions, each closed; the complementary finite union is closed, so each connected component is also open. By the connected-regular lemma these nonempty connected components are integral. Their regularity and boundary conditions are restrictions to opens: in the boundary definition retain the nonempty open restrictions of each integral component and of its intersections, whose local rings and local codimensions do not change. Their open-cover refinements remain covering by transitivity. We have proved $U(S_B,W)$. This also works in dimension zero and for an empty boundary.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, p.44, connected regular neighborhoods; boundary restriction is immediate from its definition

proof.text: Now let $S$ be as in the bounded conclusion and fix $s\in S$. Its local ring $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is reduced by definition and quasi-excellent by localization of a quasi-excellent affine chart. A prime chain in $R$ is a specialization chain in $S$, so $\dim R\leq d$. Preparation gives the excellent henselization $H=R^h$ and a finite surjective birational componentwise normalization $\coprod_a\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to\operatorname{Spec}H$, with $B_a$ normal excellent henselian local and $\dim B_a\leq\dim H=\dim R\leq d$. The preimages of $Z$ are nowhere dense. Steps 1--4 give the required finite regular marked cover over each $B_a$. The normalization is finite, hence proper, and is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/\operatorname{Spec}H$ because it is componentwise birational. It is therefore a covering generator. The finite disjoint family of its factors is a Zariski cover. Compose their regular marked coverings by the topology's transitivity axiom, obtaining a finite ordinary alteration cover of $\operatorname{Spec}H$. The sources and boundary supports are unchanged. Finite type is preserved under composition; generic points map to generic points and the residue-field extensions remain finite because they are towers of finite extensions.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, pp.43--44, henselian and finite normalization reductions; II Proposition 4.3.3, p.33

proof.text: Spread this specified cover of $\operatorname{Spec}H$ by ordinary henselian regular-pair spreading. It yields a pointed etale neighborhood $e_s:S_s\to S$ with an unchanged residue field at the chosen point over $s$, and a finite regular marked ordinary cover over $S_s$. As $s$ varies these etale neighborhoods are completely decomposed pointwise. The finite-subcover lemma extracts finitely many that are still completely decomposed, and in particular jointly surjective. They form an ordinary covering generator. Composing the finite covers over these neighborhoods gives a finite ordinary cover of $S$, with regular sources and boundaries supported exactly over $Z$. Finite type of the composites follows from composition; the spreading lemma makes $S_s\to S$ an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, so the finite generic residue extensions compose. Split the regular sources into nonempty integral connected components as in Step 4. This proves $U(S,Z)$. For $S=\varnothing$, use the allowed empty family.

source.place: II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, pp.33--34; III Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44; II Corollary 2.2.4, p.27

proof.text: For the unbounded assertion repeat Steps 5--6 separately at each $s$. The Noetherian local ring $R$ has finite dimension; preparation gives finitely many $B_a$ of dimension at most $\dim R$, and completion preserves their dimensions. Thus the hypothesis in every finite dimension permits all applications of Steps 1--4. Finite extraction in Step 6 still applies to the Noetherian scheme $S$, independently of the supremum of these local dimensions. No bound on the dimensions of the finite type approximation algebras or of the etale neighborhoods is used.

source.place: VII 2.1--2.3, p.81; II Proposition 4.3.3, pp.33--34; III Proposition 6.2, pp.43--45
